newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian fuel oil trades at five-year peak.
newsitem.headline: Asian fuel oil trades at five-year peak.

text.p: Fuel oil traded on the Singapore international market on Wednesday at its highest level since the 1991 Gulf War, traders said.
The fuel oil price has been rising sharply in recent days in line with a global rally in crude oil and petroleum products prices.
Fuel oil is used to fuel power generators and for fuelling large ships.
The main force behind the global rally has been demand for distillates, which include diesel and jet fuel.

Distillate stocks in the United States and Europe have fallen sharply heading into the peak demand fourth quarter, when stocks are usually rising. At the end of last week, U.S. stocks were 17 million barrels lower than the same time in 1995.
The new high in Singapore came after 20,000 tonnes of 180-centistoke fuel oil was sold by oil major Royal/Dutch Shell to Singapore trader Sanko Oil for $124.00 per tonne, the traders said.
The deal surpassed the previous five-year high price of $123.50 per tonne, traded in January.
Singapore gas oil, a fuel used for transport, farming, heating and power generation, also traded on Wednesday at a five-year high. It traded at $29.80 per barrel, matching a level reached on Tuesday.
Gas oil futures in London and heating oil futures in New York have been trading at five-year highs in recent weeks.

Oil benchmark Brent North Sea crude futures hit a five-year high on Tuesday and West Texas Intermediate crude futures in New York, another benchmark, traded just 10 cents short of five-year highs on Tuesday.
